title.zh: 卷五十九 列傳第四十九 江淹 任昉 王僧孺
title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 49: Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru
title.raw: 卷五十九 列傳第四十九 江淹 任昉 王僧孺 Volume 59 Biographies 49: Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十九

translations.literal: Biography 49
translations.idiomatic: Biography Forty-Nine

sentences.zh: 江淹任昉王僧孺

translations.literal: Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, and Wang Sengru

sentences.zh: 江淹字文通，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, styled Wentong, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父康之，南沙令，雅有才思。

translations.literal: His father Kangzhi was magistrate of Nansha and was elegantly gifted in literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kangzhi had served as magistrate of Nansha and possessed refined literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 淹少孤貧，常慕司馬長卿、梁伯鸞之為人，不事章句之學，留情于文章。

translations.literal: Yan was orphaned young and poor, often admired the character of Sima Xiangru and Liang Bozhuan, did not pursue exegetical commentary, and devoted his heart to literary writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan lost his father early and grew up in poverty. He admired the lives of Sima Xiangru and Liang Bozhuan, shunned pedantic textual study, and devoted himself to literature.

sentences.zh: 早為高平檀超所知，常升以上席，甚加禮焉。

translations.literal: Early on he was recognized by Tan Chao of Gaoping, who often elevated him to the upper seat and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoping scholar Tan Chao noticed him early and regularly honored him with a place at the head of the table.

sentences.zh: 起家南徐州從事，轉奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as an aide in South Xuzhou, then was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a staff aide in South Xuzhou and was later appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素好士，淹隨景素在南兗州。

translations.literal: The Song prince of Jianping, Liu Jingsu, loved scholars; Yan followed Jingsu to South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingsu of Jianping under the Song dynasty was a patron of talent, and Yan accompanied him to South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣陵令郭彥文得罪，辭連淹，言受金，淹被系獄。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Guangling, Guo Yanwen, offended authority; his deposition implicated Yan, alleging that Yan had accepted gold; Yan was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangling magistrate Guo Yanwen fell afoul of the authorities, Yan was implicated in the indictment on a charge of taking bribes and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 自獄中上書曰：

translations.literal: From prison he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: From his cell he addressed a memorial to the prince:

sentences.zh: 昔者，賤臣叩心，飛霜擊于燕地；

translations.literal: In former days, a mean subject struck his heart in anguish, and flying frost fell upon the land of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago a lowly subject, heart-stricken with grief, moved heaven until frost fell on the land of Yan;

sentences.zh: 庶女告天，振風襲于齊台。

translations.literal: a commoner's daughter appealed to Heaven, and stirring winds struck the terrace of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: and a common girl's cry to heaven brought raging winds upon the Qi terrace.

sentences.zh: 下官每讀其書，未嘗不廢卷流涕。

translations.literal: Your humble servant, whenever he reads those accounts, has never failed to set down the book and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read those stories, I cannot help but lay down the book and weep.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 士有一定之論，女有不易之行。

translations.literal: A gentleman has a fixed standard of judgment; a woman has conduct that does not change.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman holds to a fixed standard of judgment, and a woman to conduct that does not waver.

sentences.zh: 信而見疑，貞而為戮，是以壯夫義士伏死而不顧者以此也。

translations.literal: To be trusted yet suspected, to be loyal yet executed—this is why stalwart men and men of principle lie down to die without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: To be trusted yet suspected, loyal yet put to death—this is why brave and righteous men will face death without a backward glance.

sentences.zh: 下官聞仁不可恃，善不可依，謂徒虛語，乃今知之。

translations.literal: Your humble servant heard that benevolence cannot be relied upon and goodness cannot be depended on; he took these as empty words, but now he knows them to be true.
translations.idiomatic: I had heard that benevolence cannot be relied upon and goodness cannot be depended on, and I took those words for empty talk—but now I know them to be true.

sentences.zh: 伏願大王暫停左右，少加矜察。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and beg the Great Prince to pause those at his side and grant a little compassionate scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to pause a moment and grant me a little compassionate scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 下官本蓬戶桑樞之人，布衣韋帶之士，退不飾詩書以驚愚，進不買聲名於天下。

translations.literal: Your humble servant was originally one of wicker doors and mulberry pivots, a man of plain cloth and leather belt; in retirement he did not adorn the Classics to startle the foolish, in advancement he did not purchase a reputation under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I was born to a humble household, a man of plain dress and simple belt. In seclusion I did not polish the Classics to dazzle the ignorant; in public life I did not buy a name in the world.

sentences.zh: 日者，謬得升降承明之闕，出入金華之殿，何嘗不局影凝嚴，側身扃禁者乎。

translations.literal: Recently, by mistake he was allowed to ascend and descend the Chenming gate-tower and enter and leave the Jinhua hall—when did he not shrink his shadow and hold himself rigid, turning sidelong within barred prohibitions?
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, by some mistake, I was admitted to the Chenming gate-tower and the Jinhua hall. Did I ever fail to shrink my shadow, hold myself rigid, and walk sideways within those barred precincts?

sentences.zh: 竊慕大王之義，復為門下之賓，備鳴盜淺術之餘，豫三五賤伎之末。

translations.literal: Privately admiring the Great Prince's righteousness, he again became a guest at his gate, supplied with the leavings of shallow arts like the crowing thief, admitted among the lowest of petty skills.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring Your Highness's sense of honor, I became a guest at your gate again, offering what little skill I had among the humblest of petty talents.

sentences.zh: 大王惠以恩光，顧以顏色，實佩荊卿黃金之賜，竊感豫讓國士之分矣。

translations.literal: The Great Prince bestowed the light of grace and looked upon him with favor; he truly wore the gift of Jing Ke's gold and privately felt the bond of Yu Rang with his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness favored me with grace and a kind face; I truly felt the gift of Jing Ke's gold and privately sensed the bond of Yu Rang with his lord.

sentences.zh: 常欲結纓伏劍，少謝萬一，剖心摩踵，以報所天。

translations.literal: He constantly wished to tie his cap-strings and lie down with his sword, to repay in the smallest measure, to split his heart and rub his heels, to repay the one to whom he owed his life.
translations.idiomatic: I always wished to tie my cap-strings and lay down my life with my sword, to repay even the smallest fraction of your kindness, to split my heart and wear down my heels in service to the lord to whom I owed my life.

sentences.zh: 不圖小人固陋，坐貽謗缺，跡墜昭憲，身限幽圄，履影吊心，酸鼻痛骨。

translations.literal: He did not expect that base and narrow men would sit and bring slander and fault; his footsteps fell from the bright statutes, his person was confined in a dark prison; treading his shadow he mourned his heart, his nose ached with acid, his bones with pain.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined that petty and narrow men would bring slander upon me. My name has fallen from the bright law; my body is shut in a dark prison. I tread my shadow and mourn in my heart; my nose stings and my bones ache.

sentences.zh: 下官聞虧名為辱，虧形次之，是以每一念來，忽若有遺；

translations.literal: Your humble servant heard that to lose one's name is disgrace and to lose one's person comes next; therefore whenever such a thought comes, suddenly it is as if something were lost;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to lose one's good name is disgrace, and to lose one's person comes next. Whenever such a thought comes, I feel as if something vital has slipped away;

sentences.zh: 加以涉旬月，迫季秋，天光沈陰，左右無色，身非木石，與獄吏為伍。

translations.literal: Added to this, it has passed ten days and months, pressing into late autumn; the sky's light is sunk in gloom, those at his sides have no color; his person is not wood or stone—he is ranked with the prison officers.
translations.idiomatic: and now ten days and more have passed, late autumn is upon us, the sky is sunk in gloom, and those around me are ashen. I am not wood or stone—I am herded with the jailers.

sentences.zh: 此少卿所以仰天捶心，泣盡而繼之以血者也。

translations.literal: This is why Junior Grandee raised his face to heaven and beat his heart, weeping until his tears were spent and then continuing with blood.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the Junior Grand Historian raised his face to heaven and beat his breast, weeping until his tears were spent and then weeping blood.

sentences.zh: 下官雖乏鄉曲之譽，然嘗聞君子之行矣：其上則隱於簾肆之間，臥於岩石之下；

translations.literal: Your humble servant, though lacking village and lane reputation, has yet heard of the gentleman's conduct: at its highest he hides between curtain and shop, lies beneath the rocks;
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack local renown, I have heard how a gentleman conducts himself: at the highest he may hide between shop and curtain or lie beneath the cliffs;

sentences.zh: 次則結綬金馬之庭，高議雲台之上；

translations.literal: next he ties his girdle in the court of golden horses and debates loftily upon the Cloud Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: next he may tie his girdle in the court of golden horses and debate loftily upon the Cloud Terrace;

sentences.zh: 退則虜南越之君，系單于之頸。

translations.literal: in retirement he captures the lord of Nanyue and binds the Xiongnu chanyu's neck.
translations.idiomatic: in retirement he may capture the lord of Nanyue or bind the Xiongnu chanyu by the neck.

sentences.zh: 俱啟丹冊，並圖青史。

translations.literal: All alike open the red registers and are pictured in the green histories.
translations.idiomatic: All alike enter the red registers and are inscribed in the green histories.

sentences.zh: 寧爭分寸之末，競錐刀之利哉！

translations.literal: Would they contend for the tip of an inch or compete for the profit of an awl and knife!
translations.idiomatic: Would they wrangle over the tip of an inch or fight for the profit of an awl's edge!

sentences.zh: 下官聞積毀銷金，積讒摩骨，遠則直生取疑于盜金，近則伯魚被名於不義。

translations.literal: Your humble servant heard that accumulated slander melts gold and accumulated calumny wears away bone; in the distant past Zhi Sheng was suspected over stolen gold, in recent times Boyu was branded with the name of unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that accumulated slander can melt gold and accumulated calumny can wear away bone. Long ago Zhi Sheng was suspected of stealing gold; not long ago Boyu was stained with the name of unrighteousness.

sentences.zh: 彼之二才，猶或如是，況在下官，焉能自免？

translations.literal: Those two talents were still thus—how much more your humble servant: how could he exempt himself?
translations.idiomatic: If such men as those could not escape, how could someone like me hope to be spared?

sentences.zh: 昔上將之恥，絳侯幽獄，名臣之羞，史遷下室，至如下官，當何言哉。

translations.literal: In former days the shame of the supreme general, the Marquis of Jiang imprisoned in darkness; the disgrace of a famed minister, Shi Qian cast into the lower chamber—to one such as your humble servant, what can be said?
translations.idiomatic: In former days the supreme general knew shame when the Marquis of Jiang was cast into prison; a famed minister knew disgrace when Sima Qian was thrown into the lower chamber. As for someone like me, what words are left?

sentences.zh: 夫以魯連之智，辭祿而不反，接輿之賢，行歌而忘歸，子陵閉關於東越，仲蔚杜門于西秦，亦良可知也。

translations.literal: For one with the wisdom of Lu Lian to decline salary and not return, the worth of Jieyu to walk singing and forget to come home, Ziling to shut his gate in Eastern Yue, Zhongwei to block his door in Western Qin—all this may well be understood.
translations.idiomatic: When a man as wise as Lu Lian declines office and does not return, when Jieyu walks singing and forgets to come home, when Ziling shuts his gate in Eastern Yue and Zhongwei bars his door in Western Qin—the reasons are not hard to understand.

sentences.zh: 若使下官事非其虛，罪得其實，亦當鉗口吞舌，伏匕首以殞身，何以見齊魯奇節之人，燕趙悲歌之士乎。

translations.literal: If your humble servant's affair were not empty and his crime matched the facts, he too should clamp his mouth and swallow his tongue, lie down with a dagger and end his life—how could he face the men of strange integrity in Qi and Lu, the men of mournful song in Yan and Zhao?
translations.idiomatic: If my case were not false and my guilt were real, I too should clamp my mouth, swallow my tongue, and fall on a dagger to end my life. How could I face the men of strange integrity in Qi and Lu or the men of mournful song in Yan and Zhao?

sentences.zh: 方今聖曆欽明，天下樂業，青雲浮洛，榮光塞河，西洎臨洮、狄道，北距飛狐、陽原，莫不寖仁沐義，照景飲醴，而下官抱痛圜門，含憤獄戶，一物之微，有足悲者。

translations.literal: Now the sacred reign is reverent and bright, all under heaven rejoice in their work; azure clouds float over Luo, glory fills the river; west to Lintao and Didao, north to Flying Fox and Yangyuan—none do not steep in benevolence and bathe in righteousness, reflect the light and drink the sweet wine—yet your humble servant embraces pain at the round gate and holds wrath in the prison door; the slightest thing has cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacred reign is bright and all under heaven rejoice in their labors. Azure clouds float over Luoyang and glory fills the Yellow River. From Lintao and Didao in the west to Flying Fox and Yangyuan in the north, none fail to steep in benevolence and bathe in righteousness—yet I embrace pain at the prison gate and hold wrath within the jail. Even the smallest thing here is cause for grief.

sentences.zh: 仰惟大王少垂明白，則梧丘之魂不愧于沈首，鵠亭之鬼無恨於灰骨。

translations.literal: Looking up, he begs the Great Prince to let fall a little clear understanding; then the soul of Wuzhi Mound would not be ashamed before the sunken head, and the ghost of Swan Pavilion would have no regret upon its ashen bones.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to grant a little clear understanding, so that the soul at Wuzhi Mound need not be ashamed before the drowned head, and the ghost at Swan Pavilion need not regret its ashen bones.

sentences.zh: 景素覽書，即日出之。

translations.literal: Jingsu read the memorial and released him that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu read the memorial and had him released that same day.

sentences.zh: 尋舉南徐州秀才，對策上第，再遷府主簿。

translations.literal: Soon after he was nominated as a provincial graduate of South Xuzhou, ranked at the top in the policy examination, and was twice promoted to chief clerk of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was nominated as a provincial graduate of South Xuzhou, placed at the top of the policy examination, and twice promoted to chief clerk of the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 景素為荊州，淹從之鎮。

translations.literal: When Jingsu was assigned to Jingzhou, Yan followed him to the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu was posted to Jingzhou, Yan accompanied him to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，多失德，景素專據上流，咸勸因此舉事。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor ascended the throne, he committed many faults in virtue; Jingsu held exclusive control of the upper reaches, and all urged that he take action on this account.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor came to the throne, his conduct was often improper. Jingsu held the upper Yangzi region in his grip, and many urged him to raise arms on that account.

sentences.zh: 淹每從容進諫，景素不納。

translations.literal: Yan each time advanced remonstrance at his ease; Jingsu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan repeatedly offered calm remonstrance, but Jingsu would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及鎮京口，淹為鎮軍參軍，領南東海郡丞。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Jingkou, Yan served as aide to the Pacification Army and concurrently as assistant magistrate of South Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu took up his post at Jingkou, Yan served as aide to the Pacification Army and concurrently as assistant magistrate of South Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 景素與腹心日夜謀議，淹知禍機將發，乃贈詩十五首以諷焉。

translations.literal: Jingsu with his inner circle plotted day and night; Yan knew that the moment of disaster was about to break forth and therefore presented fifteen poems as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu plotted day and night with his closest confidants. Yan saw that disaster was about to break forth and presented fifteen poems as admonition.

sentences.zh: 會東海太守陸澄丁艱，淹自謂郡丞應行郡事，景素用司馬柳世隆。

translations.literal: It happened that the grand administrator of Donghai, Lu Cheng, entered mourning for a parent; Yan considered that as assistant magistrate he should act in the commandery's affairs, but Jingsu employed the marshal Liu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: When Donghai grand administrator Lu Cheng entered mourning for a parent, Yan assumed that as assistant magistrate he should act in the commandery's affairs, but Jingsu appointed the marshal Liu Shilong instead.

sentences.zh: 淹固求之，景素大怒，言於選部，黜為建安吳興令。

translations.literal: Yan firmly pressed his claim; Jingsu was greatly angered and spoke to the selection office, demoting him to magistrate of Jian'an in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan pressed his claim firmly. Jingsu was furious and spoke to the selection office, demoting him to magistrate of Jian'an in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 及齊高帝輔政，聞其才，召為尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi served as regent, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Director of the Imperial Carriage Office in the Secretariat and as aide in the Rapid Cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi served as regent, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Director of the Imperial Carriage Office in the Secretariat and as aide in the Rapid Cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？」

translations.literal: Before long the inspector of Jingzhou, Shen Youzhi, raised rebellion; Emperor Gao said to Yan, "All under heaven is in turmoil like this—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingzhou inspector Shen Youzhi rose in rebellion. Emperor Gao asked Yan, "The realm is in turmoil like this—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「昔項強而劉弱，袁眾而曹寡，羽卒受一劍之辱，紹終為奔北之虜，此所謂'在德不在鼎'，公何疑哉。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "In former days Xiang was strong and Liu weak, Yuan had many and Cao few; Yu ended by suffering the humiliation of a single sword, Shao in the end became a captive fleeing north—this is what is called 'virtue lies not in the tripod.' Why should Your Lordship doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Long ago Xiang Yu was strong and Liu Bang weak, Yuan Shao had many men and Cao Cao few. Yu ended by suffering the humiliation of a single sword-stroke, and Shao in the end became a captive fleeing north. As the saying goes, 'virtue lies not in the tripod.' Why should you doubt?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「試為我言之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Try to explain it for me."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Explain it for me."

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「公雄武有奇略，一勝也；

translations.literal: Yan said, "Your Lordship is heroically martial with a singular strategy—one victory;
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Your Lordship is heroically martial with a singular strategy—that is one victory;

sentences.zh: 寬容而仁恕，二勝也；

translations.literal: tolerant, generous, and forgiving—two victories;
translations.idiomatic: you are tolerant, generous, and forgiving—that is two;

sentences.zh: 賢能畢力，三勝也；

translations.literal: the worthy and able exert all their strength—three victories;
translations.idiomatic: the worthy and able exert all their strength—that is three;

sentences.zh: 人望所歸，四勝也；

translations.literal: the people's hopes turn to you—four victories;
translations.idiomatic: the people's hopes turn to you—that is four;

sentences.zh: 奉天子而伐叛逆，五勝也。

translations.literal: upholding the Son of Heaven while attacking rebels—five victories.
translations.idiomatic: you uphold the Son of Heaven while attacking rebels—that is five.

sentences.zh: 彼志銳而器小，一敗也；

translations.literal: On their side, their will is sharp but their capacity small—one defeat;
translations.idiomatic: On their side, their will is sharp but their capacity small—that is one defeat;

sentences.zh: 有威無恩，二敗也；

translations.literal: they have authority but no grace—two defeats;
translations.idiomatic: they have authority but no grace—that is two;

sentences.zh: 士卒解體，三敗也；

translations.literal: the soldiers' bodies dissolve in disunity—three defeats;
translations.idiomatic: their soldiers are falling apart—that is three;

sentences.zh: 搢紳不懷，四敗也；

translations.literal: the gentry do not embrace them—four defeats;
translations.idiomatic: the gentry do not embrace them—that is four;

sentences.zh: 懸兵數千里、而無同惡相濟，五敗也。

translations.literal: they hang their army thousands of li away without like-minded men to aid one another—five defeats.
translations.idiomatic: they hang their army thousands of li away without allies to aid one another—that is five.

sentences.zh: 雖豺狼十萬，而終為我獲焉。」

translations.literal: Though they be a hundred thousand wolves and jackals, in the end they will be taken by us."
translations.idiomatic: Though they field a hundred thousand wolves and jackals, in the end they will be ours."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「君談過矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Your talk goes too far."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "You go too far."

sentences.zh: 桂陽之役，朝廷周章，詔檄久之未就。

translations.literal: In the Guiyang campaign the court was in confusion; the proclamation and call to arms long went unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guiyang campaign the court was in disarray, and the proclamation and call to arms long remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝引淹入中書省，先賜酒食，淹素能飲啖，食鵝炙垂盡，進酒數升訖，文誥亦辦。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi led Yan into the Secretariat, first bestowing wine and food; Yan had always been able to drink and eat heartily—he ate the roast goose nearly to the end, advanced several sheng of wine, and when that was done the documents were also finished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi brought Yan into the Secretariat, first offering wine and food. Yan had always been a hearty drinker and eater. He nearly finished a plate of roast goose, drank several sheng of wine, and by the time he was done the documents were finished as well.

sentences.zh: 相府建，補記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Chancellor's office was established, he was appointed recorder-aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chancellor's office was established, he was appointed recorder-aide.

sentences.zh: 高帝讓九錫及諸章表，皆淹制也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao's declination of the Nine Bestowals and all the memorials and tables were composed by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao's declination of the Nine Bestowals and all the memorials and tables were composed by Yan.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，復為驃騎豫章王嶷記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he again served as recorder-aide to Prince Yao of Yuzhang in the Rapid Cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he again served as recorder-aide to Prince Yao of Yuzhang in the Rapid Cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，始置史官，淹與司徒左長史檀超共掌其任，所為條例，並為王儉所駁，其言不行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan the historiographical office was first established; Yan together with Tan Chao, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, jointly held that charge; the regulations they drafted were all rejected by Wang Jian, and their proposals were not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan the historiographical office was first established. Yan and Tan Chao, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, jointly held that charge. The regulations they drafted were all rejected by Wang Jian, and their proposals were not implemented.

sentences.zh: 淹任性文雅，不以著述在懷，所撰十三篇竟無次序。

translations.literal: Yan was by nature free and refined in letters, did not keep composition in his heart, and the thirteen chapters he wrote in the end had no order.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was by nature free-spirited and refined in letters and did not take composition to heart. The thirteen chapters he wrote in the end had no order.

sentences.zh: 又領東武令，參掌詔策。

translations.literal: He also held the post of magistrate of Dongwu and participated in drafting edicts and policies.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as magistrate of Dongwu and participated in drafting edicts and policies.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書侍郎，王儉嘗謂曰：「卿年三十五，已為中書侍郎，才學如此，何憂不至尚書金紫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wang Jian once said to him, "You are thirty-five and already Vice Director of the Secretariat; with talent and learning such as this, why worry that you will not reach Minister and golden seal and purple cord?
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat. Wang Jian once told him, "You are thirty-five and already Vice Director of the Secretariat. With talent and learning such as yours, why worry that you will not reach Minister and the golden seal and purple cord?

sentences.zh: 所謂富貴卿自取之，但問年壽何如爾。」

translations.literal: What is called wealth and honor you will take for yourself—only ask how your years of life will be."
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and honor you will take for yourself—only ask how long you will live."

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「不悟明公見眷之重。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "I did not realize how heavily the enlightened lord favored me."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "I did not realize how heavily you favored me."

sentences.zh: 永明三年，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he concurrently served as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he concurrently served as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時襄陽人開古塚，得玉鏡及竹簡古書，字不可識。

translations.literal: At that time a man of Xiangyang opened an ancient tomb and obtained a jade mirror and bamboo slips of ancient books whose characters could not be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man of Xiangyang opened an ancient tomb and obtained a jade mirror and bamboo slips of ancient writing whose characters could not be read.

sentences.zh: 王僧虔善識字體，亦不能諳，直云似是科斗書。

translations.literal: Wang Sengqian was skilled at recognizing script forms yet could not decipher them either; he simply said they seemed to be tadpole script.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian was skilled at recognizing script forms yet could not decipher them either; he simply said they seemed to be tadpole script.

sentences.zh: 淹以科斗字推之，則周宣王之前也。

translations.literal: Yan deduced from the tadpole characters that they dated from before King Xuan of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan deduced from the tadpole characters that they dated from before King Xuan of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 簡殆如新。

translations.literal: The slips were nearly like new.
translations.idiomatic: The slips were nearly as fresh as new.

sentences.zh: 少帝初，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Young Emperor's reign he concurrently served as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Young Emperor's reign he concurrently served as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明帝作相，謂淹曰：「君昔在尚書中，非公事不妄行，在官寬猛能折衷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming served as Chancellor he said to Yan, "In former days in the Secretariat you did not act rashly except on public business; in office you could balance leniency and severity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming served as Chancellor he told Yan, "In former days in the Secretariat you did not act rashly except on public business. In office you could balance leniency and severity.

sentences.zh: 今為南司，足以振肅百僚也。」

translations.literal: Now as head of the southern bureau you are sufficient to rouse and sober the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: Now as head of the southern bureau you are fit to rouse and sober the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「今日之事，可謂當官而行，更恐不足仰稱明旨爾。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "Today's affairs may be called acting as the office requires; I fear rather that I am not sufficient to live up to your enlightened intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Today's affairs may be called acting as the office requires. I fear rather that I am not sufficient to live up to your enlightened intent."

sentences.zh: 於是彈中書令謝朏、司徒左長史王繢、護軍長史庾弘遠，並以托疾不預山陵公事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he impeached Director of the Secretariat Xie Tiao, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Hui, and Chief Clerk of the Guards General Yu Hongyuan, all for feigning illness and not participating in the mountain-tomb public business.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he impeached Director of the Secretariat Xie Tiao, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Hui, and Chief Clerk of the Guards General Yu Hongyuan, all for feigning illness and failing to take part in the imperial tomb ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 又奏收前益州刺史劉悛、梁州刺史陰智伯，並贓貨巨萬，輒收付廷尉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized for the arrest of the former inspector of Yizhou Liu Xiao and the inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zhibo, both of whom had taken bribes in the tens of thousands, and had them immediately taken and delivered to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized for the arrest of former Yizhou inspector Liu Xiao and Liangzhou inspector Yin Zhibo, both of whom had taken bribes in the tens of thousands, and had them immediately delivered to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守沈昭略、永嘉太守庾曇隆及諸郡二千石並大縣官長，多被劾，內外肅然。

translations.literal: The grand administrators of Linhai Shen Zhaolue and Yongjia Yu Tanlong, together with the two-thousand-dan officials of the various commanderies and the chiefs of great counties, were mostly impeached; within and without the court was sobered.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai grand administrator Shen Zhaolue, Yongjia grand administrator Yu Tanlong, and the two-thousand-dan officials of the various commanderies and chiefs of great counties were mostly impeached. Within and without, the court was sobered.

sentences.zh: 明帝謂曰：「自宋以來，不復有嚴明中丞，君今日可謂近世獨步。」

translations.literal: Emperor Ming said to him, "Since the Song there has not again been a stern and clear censor-in-chief; today you may be called walking alone in recent times."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming told him, "Since the Song there has not again been a stern and clear censor-in-chief. Today you may be called without peer in recent times."

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書監，侍中，衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat Library, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat Library, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 初，淹年十三時，孤貧，常采薪以養母，曾于樵所得貂蟬一具，將鬻以供養。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan was thirteen, orphaned and poor, he often gathered firewood to support his mother; once while cutting wood he obtained a set of cicada ornaments and was about to sell them to provide support.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yan was thirteen, orphaned and poor, he often gathered firewood to support his mother. Once while cutting wood he found a set of cicada ornaments and was about to sell them for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 其母曰：「此故汝之休征也，汝才行若此，豈長貧賤也，可留待得侍中著之。」

translations.literal: His mother said, "This is surely your auspicious sign; with talent and conduct such as yours, how could you long remain poor and base? Keep it and wait until you become Attendant-in-Ordinary to wear it."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "This is surely your auspicious sign. With talent and conduct such as yours, how could you long remain poor and base? Keep it and wait until you become Attendant-in-Ordinary to wear it."

sentences.zh: 至是果如母言。

translations.literal: When he reached this point it indeed came about as his mother had said.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached this point it indeed came about as his mother had said.

sentences.zh: 永元中，崔慧景舉兵圍都，衣冠悉投名刺，淹稱疾不往。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era Cui Huijing raised troops and besieged the capital; the gentry all submitted calling cards, but Yan claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongyuan era Cui Huijing raised troops and besieged the capital. The gentry all submitted calling cards, but Yan claimed illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 及事平，時人服其先見。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, men of the time admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, men of the time admired his foresight.

sentences.zh: 東昏末，淹以秘書監兼衛尉，又副領軍王瑩。

translations.literal: At the end of the Donghun era Yan served as Supervisor of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Commandant of the Guard, and also as deputy to army commander Wang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Donghun era Yan served as Supervisor of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Commandant of the Guard, and also as deputy to army commander Wang Ying.

sentences.zh: 及梁武至新林，淹微服來奔，位相國右長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang reached Xinlin, Yan came in disguise to join him and was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Chancellorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang reached Xinlin, Yan came in disguise to join him and was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Chancellorate.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，為散騎常侍、左衛將軍，封臨沮縣伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linju county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linju county.

sentences.zh: 淹乃謂子弟曰：「吾本素宦，不求富貴，今之忝竊，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Yan then said to his sons and younger brothers: "I was always a modest official and sought no wealth or honor. Today's undeserved elevation has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then said to his sons and younger brothers: "I was always a modest official and sought no wealth or honor. Today's undeserved elevation has reached this point.

sentences.zh: 平生言止足之事，亦以備矣。

translations.literal: What I said all my life about knowing when to stop is now complete.
translations.idiomatic: What I said all my life about knowing when to stop is now complete.

sentences.zh: 人生行樂，須富貴何時。

translations.literal: Life is for enjoying oneself—must one wait for wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Life is for enjoying oneself—must one wait for wealth and honor?

sentences.zh: 吾功名既立，正欲歸身草萊耳。」

translations.literal: My merit and fame are established, and I only wish to return to common life."
translations.idiomatic: My merit and fame are established, and I only wish to return to common life."

sentences.zh: 以疾遷金紫光祿大夫，改封醴陵伯，卒。

translations.literal: Due to illness he was transferred to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, enfeoffed anew as Marquis of Liling, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Due to illness he was transferred to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, enfeoffed anew as Marquis of Liling, and died.

sentences.zh: 武帝為素服舉哀，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wore plain mourning and held mourning rites for him; his posthumous name was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wore plain mourning and held mourning rites for him; his posthumous name was Xian.

sentences.zh: 淹少以文章顯，晚節才思微退，云為宣城太守時罷歸，始泊禪靈寺渚，夜夢一人自稱張景陽，謂曰：「前以一匹錦相寄，今可見還。」

translations.literal: Yan was early distinguished by his literary writings; in his later years his talent and thought slightly declined. It is said that when he was dismissed and returned after serving as grand administrator of Xuancheng, he first moored at the Chanling Temple ford; at night he dreamed of a man who called himself Zhang Jingyang, who said, "Before I entrusted a bolt of brocade to you; now you may return it."
translations.idiomatic: Yan won early fame through his writings, but in his later years his talent and inspiration declined slightly. It is said that when he was dismissed and returned after serving as grand administrator of Xuancheng, he first moored at the Chanling Temple ford. At night he dreamed of a man who called himself Zhang Jingyang, who said, "I once entrusted a bolt of brocade to you. You may return it now."

sentences.zh: 淹探懷中得數尺與之，此人大恚曰：「那得割截都盡。」

translations.literal: Yan reached into his bosom, took out several feet, and gave them to him; the man was greatly angered and said, "How could you cut it all away!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan reached into his bosom, took out several feet, and gave them to him. The man was furious and said, "How could you cut it all away!"

sentences.zh: 顧見丘遲謂曰：「餘此數尺既無所用，以遺君。」

translations.literal: Turning, he saw Qiu Chi and said to him, "These few feet that remain are of no use to me; I give them to you."
translations.idiomatic: Turning, he saw Qiu Chi and said to him, "These few feet that remain are of no use to me. I give them to you."

sentences.zh: 自爾淹文章躓矣。

translations.literal: From then on Yan's literary writings stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yan's literary writings stumbled.

sentences.zh: 又嘗宿於冶亭，夢一丈夫自稱郭璞，謂淹曰：「吾有筆在卿處多年，可以見還。」

translations.literal: He also once lodged at Yeting and dreamed of a man who called himself Guo Pu, who said to Yan, "I have had a brush at your place for many years; you may return it now."
translations.idiomatic: He also once lodged at Yeting and dreamed of a man who called himself Guo Pu, who said to Yan, "I have had a brush at your place for many years. You may return it now."

sentences.zh: 淹乃探懷中得五色筆一以授之。

translations.literal: Yan then reached into his bosom, took out one five-colored brush, and handed it over.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then reached into his bosom, took out one five-colored brush, and handed it over.

sentences.zh: 爾後為詩絕無美句，時人謂之才盡。

translations.literal: After that, in composing poetry he had absolutely no fine lines; men of the time said his talent was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After that his poetry had no fine lines at all, and men of the time said his talent was spent.

sentences.zh: 凡所著述，自撰為前後集，並齊史十志，並行於世。

translations.literal: All that he wrote he compiled into earlier and later collections, together with the Ten Monographs of Qi history, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he wrote he compiled into earlier and later collections, together with the Ten Monographs of Qi history, all of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲為赤縣經以補山海之闕，竟不成。

translations.literal: He once wished to compose a Classic of the Red Counties to supplement the gaps in the Classic of Mountains and Seas, but in the end did not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: He once wished to compose a Classic of the Red Counties to fill the gaps in the Classic of Mountains and Seas, but never finished it.

sentences.zh: 子蒍嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wei succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 任昉字彥升，樂安博昌人也。

translations.literal: Ren Fang, courtesy name Yansheng, was a native of Bochang in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang, styled Yansheng, came from Bochang in Le'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 父遙，齊中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yao was Palace Attendant of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao served as Palace Attendant under Qi.

sentences.zh: 遙兄遐字景遠，少敦學業，家行甚謹，位御史中丞、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yao's elder brother Xia, courtesy name Jingyuan, in youth devoted himself to learning; his household conduct was very strict; he reached the posts of Censor-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's elder brother Xia, styled Jingyuan, devoted himself to learning from youth. His household conduct was very strict. He rose to Censor-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.

sentences.zh: 永明中，遐以罪將徙荒裔，遙懷名請訴，言淚交下，齊武帝聞而哀之，竟得免。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era Xia was for a crime about to be banished to the remote borderlands; Yao, cherishing his name, pleaded in appeal, words and tears mingling; Emperor Wu of Qi heard and pitied him, and in the end he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era Xia was about to be banished to the remote borderlands for a crime. Yao pleaded in appeal on his behalf, words and tears mingling. Emperor Wu of Qi heard and pitied him, and in the end Xia was spared.

sentences.zh: 遙妻河東裴氏，高明有德行，嘗晝臥，夢有五色采旗蓋四角懸鈴，自天而墜，其一鈴落入懷中，心悸因而有娠。

translations.literal: Yao's wife, the Pei clan of Hedong, was lofty and bright in virtue; once while sleeping by day she dreamed of a five-colored banner-canopy with bells hung at the four corners falling from heaven; one bell fell into her bosom; her heart palpitated and she became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's wife, of the Pei clan of Hedong, was a woman of lofty virtue. Once while sleeping by day she dreamed of a five-colored banner-canopy with bells at the four corners falling from heaven. One bell fell into her bosom. Her heart palpitated and she became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 占者曰：「必生才子。」

translations.literal: The diviner said, "She will surely bear a talented son."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said, "She will surely bear a talented son."

sentences.zh: 及生昉，身長七尺五寸，幼而聰敏，早稱神悟。

translations.literal: When Fang was born, his height was seven feet five inches; in youth he was clever and keen, and early was called divinely perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang was born, he stood seven feet five inches tall. Even as a child he was clever and keen, and early on was called divinely perceptive.

sentences.zh: 四歲誦詩數十篇，八歲能屬文，自製月儀，辭義甚美。

translations.literal: At four he could recite several tens of poems; at eight he could compose prose; he himself made a Monthly Ritual, its language and meaning very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: At four he could recite dozens of poems. At eight he could compose prose and wrote a Monthly Ritual of his own, its language and meaning very fine.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回嘗謂遙曰：「聞卿有令子，相為喜之。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui once said to Yao, "I hear you have an excellent son; I rejoice with you.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui once told Yao, "I hear you have an excellent son. I rejoice with you.

sentences.zh: 所謂百不為多，一不為少。」

translations.literal: What is called: a hundred is not too many, one is not too few."
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, a hundred is not too many, and one is not too few."

sentences.zh: 由是聞聲藉甚。

translations.literal: From this his fame by report became very great.
translations.idiomatic: From this his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 年十二，從叔晷有知人之量，見而稱其小名曰：「阿堆，吾家千里駒也。」

translations.literal: At twelve, his paternal uncle's son Gao had the measure to know men; seeing him he praised his childhood name, saying, "A-Dui, our family's thousand-li colt!"
translations.idiomatic: At twelve his cousin Gao, who had the measure to know men, saw him and praised his childhood name, saying, "A-Dui, our family's thousand-li colt!"

sentences.zh: 昉孝友純至，每侍親疾，衣不解帶，言與淚並，湯藥飲食必先經口。

translations.literal: Fang was pure and utmost in filial piety and brotherly love; whenever he attended a parent's illness he did not undo his belt, words and tears together; broth, medicine, drink, and food he always tasted first.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was pure and utmost in filial piety and brotherly love. Whenever he attended a parent's illness he did not undo his belt, and words and tears came together. Broth, medicine, drink, and food he always tasted first.

sentences.zh: 初為奉朝請，舉兗州秀才，拜太學博士。

translations.literal: He first served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, was nominated as a provincial graduate of Yanzhou, and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, was nominated as a provincial graduate of Yanzhou, and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引為主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming the Guards General Wang Jian served concurrently as Administrator of Danyang and again brought him in as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongming, Guards General Wang Jian served concurrently as Administrator of Danyang and again brought him in as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 儉每見其文，必三復殷勤，以為當時無輩，曰：「自傅季友以來，始復見於任子。

translations.literal: Whenever Jian saw his writings he would read them three times with earnest care, considering that in the present age there was no equal, and said, "Since Fu Jiyou, one sees this again in Master Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jian saw his writings he would read them three times with earnest care, considering that in the present age there was no equal. He said, "Since Fu Jiyou, one sees this again in Master Ren.

sentences.zh: 若孔門是用，其入室升堂。」

translations.literal: If the gate of Confucius were to employ him, he would enter the inner chamber and ascend the hall."
translations.idiomatic: If the gate of Confucius were to employ him, he would enter the inner chamber and ascend the hall."

sentences.zh: 於是令昉作一文，及見，曰：「正得吾腹中之欲。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Fang compose a piece of writing, and when he saw it said, "This is exactly what was in my belly's desire."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had Fang compose a piece of writing, and when he saw it said, "This is exactly what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 乃出自作文，令昉點正，昉因定數位。

translations.literal: He then brought out a composition of his own and had Fang mark and correct it; Fang thereupon fixed several places.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought out a composition of his own and had Fang mark and correct it. Fang fixed several places.

sentences.zh: 儉拊幾歎曰：「後世誰知子定吾文！」

translations.literal: Jian struck the table and sighed, "Who in later ages will know that you fixed my writing!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian struck the table and sighed, "Who in later ages will know that you fixed my writing!"

sentences.zh: 其見知如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he known and appreciated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he known and appreciated.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒竟陵王記室參軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.

sentences.zh: 時琅邪王融有才俊，自謂無對當時，見昉之文，怳然自失。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance; he considered himself without rival in the age; when he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance and considered himself without rival in the age. When he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.

sentences.zh: 以父喪去官，泣血三年，杖而後起。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; he wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he left office. He wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝謂昉伯遐曰：「聞昉哀瘠過禮，使人憂之，非直亡卿之寶，亦時才可惜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi said to Fang's elder uncle Xia, "I hear Fang's mourning emaciation exceeds the rites and causes one worry; it is not only the loss of your treasure but also a pity for the talent of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi told Fang's elder uncle Xia, "I hear Fang's mourning emaciation exceeds the rites and causes worry. It is not only the loss of your treasure but also a pity for the talent of the age.

sentences.zh: 宜深相全譬。」

translations.literal: You should deeply comfort and instruct him."
translations.idiomatic: You should deeply comfort and instruct him."

sentences.zh: 遐使進飲食，當時勉勵，回即歐出。

translations.literal: Xia had food and drink brought in and at the time urged him on, but as soon as he returned he vomited it out.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had food and drink brought in and urged him on, but as soon as he returned Fang vomited it out.

sentences.zh: 昉父遙本性重檳榔，以為常餌，臨終嘗求之，剖百許口，不得好者，昉亦所嗜好，深以為恨，遂終身不嚐檳榔。

translations.literal: Fang's father Yao by nature prized betel nut as a regular food; on his deathbed he once asked for it; they split open a hundred or so, but could not find a good one; Fang too was fond of it and deeply regretted this, and therefore never tasted betel nut for his whole life.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's father Yao prized betel nut as a regular food. On his deathbed he once asked for it, but of a hundred or so split open none was good. Fang too was fond of it and deeply regretted this, and never tasted betel nut for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，昉先以毀瘠，每一慟絕，良久乃蘇，因廬於墓側，以終喪禮。

translations.literal: When he met with mourning for his stepmother, Fang had already been emaciated by grief; each time he wailed he fainted and only after a long while revived; he therefore built a hut by the tomb and completed the mourning rites there.
translations.idiomatic: When he met with mourning for his stepmother, Fang had already been emaciated by grief. Each time he wailed he fainted and only after a long while revived. He built a hut by the tomb and completed the mourning rites there.

sentences.zh: 哭泣之地，草為不生。

translations.literal: At the place of his weeping the grass did not grow.
translations.idiomatic: At the place of his weeping the grass would not grow.

sentences.zh: 昉素強壯，腰帶甚充，服闋後不復可識。

translations.literal: Fang had always been robust; his waist belt was very full; after the mourning period ended he could no longer be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had always been robust and his waist belt very full. After the mourning period ended he could no longer be recognized.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝深加器異，欲大相擢引，為愛憎所白，乃除太子步兵校尉，掌東宮書記。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi greatly valued and distinguished him and wished to promote him to high office, but was reported by those of love and hate; he was therefore appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers for the Heir Apparent and managed the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi greatly valued and distinguished him and wished to promote him to high office, but enemies spoke against him. He was therefore appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers for the Heir Apparent and managed the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝廢郁林王，始為侍中、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、錄尚書事，封宣城郡公，使昉具草。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi deposed Prince Yulin, he first became Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Grand General of the Rapid Cavalry, Commissioner Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies with an open office, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng commandery and had Fang draft the documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi deposed Prince Yulin, he first became Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Grand General of the Rapid Cavalry, Commissioner Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies with an open office, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat. He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng commandery and had Fang draft the documents.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其辭斥，甚慍，昉亦由是終建武中位不過列校。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated the reproach in the wording and was greatly angered; Fang also for this reason to the end of Jianwu never rose above the rank of colonel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hated the reproach in the wording and was greatly angered. Fang also for this reason never rose above the rank of colonel through the end of Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 昉尤長為筆，頗慕傅亮才思無窮，當時王公表奏無不請焉。

translations.literal: Fang was especially skilled at wielding the brush and greatly admired Fu Liang's inexhaustible talent and thought; at the time there was no prince or duke memorial or report for which he was not asked.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was especially skilled at wielding the brush and greatly admired Fu Liang's inexhaustible talent. At the time there was no prince or duke memorial or report for which he was not asked.

sentences.zh: 昉起草即成，不加點竄。

translations.literal: Fang's drafts were finished as soon as written, without adding a dot or stroke of correction.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's drafts were finished as soon as written, without a dot or stroke of correction.

sentences.zh: 沈約一代辭宗，深所推挹。

translations.literal: Shen Yue, patriarch of letters for a generation, deeply esteemed and drew him up.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, patriarch of letters for a generation, deeply esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 永元中，紆意于梅蟲兒，東昏中旨用為中書郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he curried favor with Mei Chong'er; by the secret wish of the Depraved One he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongyuan era he curried favor with Mei Chong'er. By the secret wish of the Depraved Emperor he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謝尚書令王亮，亮曰：「卿宜謝梅，那忽謝我。」

translations.literal: He thanked Director of the Secretariat Wang Liang; Liang said, "You ought to thank Mei—why suddenly thank me?"
translations.idiomatic: He thanked Director of the Secretariat Wang Liang. Liang said, "You ought to thank Mei—why suddenly thank me?"

sentences.zh: 昉慚而退。

translations.literal: Fang withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Fang withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 末為司徒右長史。

translations.literal: At the end he served as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he served as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝克建鄴，霸府初開，以為驃騎記室參軍，專主文翰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took Jiankang, as the hegemon's office was first opened he was appointed recorder-aide in the Rapid Cavalry command and exclusively managed literary documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang took Jiankang, as the hegemon's office was first opened he was appointed recorder-aide in the Rapid Cavalry command and exclusively managed literary documents.

sentences.zh: 每制書草，沈約輒求同署。

translations.literal: Whenever imperial documents were drafted, Shen Yue always asked to sign jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever imperial documents were drafted, Shen Yue always asked to sign jointly.

sentences.zh: 嘗被急召，昉出而約在，是後文筆，約參制焉。

translations.literal: Once when urgently summoned, Fang went out while Yue remained; from then on in literary documents Yue participated in drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Once when urgently summoned, Fang went out while Yue remained. From then on Yue participated in drafting literary documents.

sentences.zh: 始梁武與昉遇竟陵王西邸，從容謂昉曰：「我登三府，當以卿為記室。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Emperor Wu of Liang and Fang met at Prince Jingling's Western Lodge, he said at ease to Fang, "When I ascend the Three Offices, I shall make you recorder."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Emperor Wu of Liang and Fang met at Prince Jingling's Western Lodge, he said at ease to Fang, "When I ascend the Three Offices, I shall make you recorder."

sentences.zh: 昉亦戲帝曰：「我若登三事，當以卿為騎兵。」

translations.literal: Fang also jested with the Emperor, "If I ascend the Three Affairs, I shall make you cavalry officer."
translations.idiomatic: Fang also jested with the Emperor, "If I ascend the Three Affairs, I shall make you cavalry officer."

sentences.zh: 以帝善騎也。

translations.literal: This was because the Emperor was skilled at riding.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the Emperor was skilled at riding.

sentences.zh: 至是引昉符昔言焉。

translations.literal: At this point he cited Fang in fulfillment of their former words.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he cited Fang in fulfillment of their former words.

sentences.zh: 昉奉箋云：「昔承清宴，屬有緒言，提挈之旨，形乎善謔。

translations.literal: Fang submitted a letter saying, "In former days I received a clear banquet and there was a thread of words; the intent to lift and draw one up took form in good jest.
translations.idiomatic: Fang submitted a letter saying, "In former days I received a clear banquet and there was a thread of words. The intent to lift and draw one up took form in good jest.

sentences.zh: 豈謂多幸，斯言不渝。」

translations.literal: Who would have said such great fortune—that these words would not change!"
translations.idiomatic: Who would have said such great fortune—that these words would not change!"

sentences.zh: 蓋為此也。

translations.literal: This was probably on that account.
translations.idiomatic: This was probably on that account.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，禪讓文誥，多昉所具。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, the abdication documents were mostly drafted by Fang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established, the abdication documents were mostly drafted by Fang.

sentences.zh: 奉世叔父母不異嚴親，事兄嫂恭謹。

translations.literal: He served his uncles and aunts of the generation as if they were stern parents, and attended elder brother and sister-in-law with reverent care.
translations.idiomatic: He served his uncles and aunts of the generation as if they were stern parents, and attended elder brother and sister-in-law with reverent care.

sentences.zh: 外氏貧闕，恒營奉供養。

translations.literal: His mother's clan was poor and lacking; he constantly provided for their support.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's clan was poor and lacking, and he constantly provided for their support.

sentences.zh: 祿奉所收，四方餉遺，皆班之親戚，即日便盡。

translations.literal: The salary and stipends he received, and gifts sent from the four directions, he all distributed among his kin and on the same day they were spent.
translations.idiomatic: The salary and stipends he received, and gifts sent from the four directions, he distributed among his kin and on the same day they were spent.

sentences.zh: 性通脫，不事儀形，喜慍未嘗形于色，車服亦不鮮明。

translations.literal: By nature he was free and unbound, did not attend to ceremonial form; joy and anger never showed on his face; his carriage and garments were also not bright.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was free and unbound and did not attend to ceremonial form. Joy and anger never showed on his face, and his carriage and garments were not bright.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，曆給事黃門侍郎，吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he successively served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he successively served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為義興太守。

translations.literal: He went out as grand administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 歲荒民散，以私奉米豆為粥，活三千餘人。

translations.literal: The year was famine and the people scattered; with his private stipend of rice and beans he made gruel and kept alive more than three thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: The year was famine and the people scattered. With his private stipend of rice and beans he made gruel and kept alive more than three thousand people.

sentences.zh: 時產子者不舉，昉嚴其制，罪同殺人。

translations.literal: At the time those who bore children did not raise them; Fang made the regulation strict, the crime equal to murder.
translations.idiomatic: At the time those who bore children did not raise them. Fang made the regulation strict, the crime equal to murder.

sentences.zh: 孕者供其資費，濟者千室。

translations.literal: For pregnant women he supplied their expenses; those he aided numbered a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For pregnant women he supplied their expenses. Those he aided numbered a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 在郡所得公田奉秩八百餘石，昉五分督一，余者悉原，兒妾食麥而已。

translations.literal: In the commandery the public-field stipend he received was more than eight hundred piculs; Fang took one part in five for supervision, remitted all the rest, and his sons, concubines, and servants ate only wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery the public-field stipend he received was more than eight hundred piculs. Fang took one part in five for supervision, remitted all the rest, and his sons, concubines, and servants ate only wheat.

sentences.zh: 友人彭城到溉、溉弟洽從昉共為山澤遊。

translations.literal: His friends Dao Gai of Pengcheng and Gai's younger brother Qia followed Fang on excursions to mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: His friends Dao Gai of Pengcheng and Gai's younger brother Qia followed Fang on excursions to mountains and marshes.

sentences.zh: 及被代登舟，止有絹七匹，米五石。

translations.literal: When he was replaced and boarded his boat, he had only seven bolts of silk and five piculs of rice.
translations.idiomatic: When he was replaced and boarded his boat, he had only seven bolts of silk and five piculs of rice.

sentences.zh: 至都無衣，鎮軍將軍沈約遣裙衫迎之。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he had no clothes; the Pacification Army General Shen Yue sent skirts and shirts to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he had no clothes. Pacification Army General Shen Yue sent skirts and shirts to meet him.

sentences.zh: 重除吏部郎，參掌大選，居職不稱。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel and participated in managing the great selection, but in office did not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel and participated in managing the great selection, but in office did not measure up.

sentences.zh: 尋轉御史中丞、秘書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and Director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and Director of the Secretariat Library.

sentences.zh: 自齊永元以來，秘閣四部，篇卷紛雜，昉手自讎校，由是篇目定焉。

translations.literal: Since Yongyuan of Qi, the four sections of the secret archive had volumes in disorder; Fang personally collated them, and thereby the catalogue was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongyuan of Qi the four sections of the secret archive had volumes in disorder. Fang personally collated them, and thereby the catalogue was fixed.

sentences.zh: 出為新安太守，在郡不事邊幅，率然曳杖，徒行邑郭。

translations.literal: He went out as grand administrator of Xin'an; in the commandery he did not attend to the borders of his robe, casually dragging his staff and walking on foot through the town.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand administrator of Xin'an. In the commandery he did not attend to the borders of his robe, casually dragging his staff and walking on foot through the town.

sentences.zh: 人通辭訟者，就路決焉。

translations.literal: When people came with petitions and lawsuits, he decided them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When people came with petitions and lawsuits, he decided them on the road.

sentences.zh: 為政清省，吏人便之。

translations.literal: His government was clear and sparing; officials and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: His government was clear and sparing, and officials and people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，唯有桃花米二十石，無以為斂。

translations.literal: He died in office; he had only twenty piculs of peach-blossom rice and nothing with which to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. He had only twenty piculs of peach-blossom rice and nothing with which to bury him.

sentences.zh: 遺言不許以新安一物還都，雜木為棺，浣衣為斂。

translations.literal: His testamentary words forbade taking a single thing from Xin'an back to the capital; miscellaneous wood for the coffin, washed garments for the shroud.
translations.idiomatic: His testamentary words forbade taking a single thing from Xin'an back to the capital. Miscellaneous wood served for the coffin and washed garments for the shroud.

sentences.zh: 闔境痛惜，百姓共立祠堂于城南，歲時祠之。

translations.literal: The whole territory grieved; the common people jointly erected a shrine south of the city and sacrificed to him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The whole territory grieved. The common people jointly erected a shrine south of the city and sacrificed to him at the seasons.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞問，方食西苑綠沈瓜，投之於盤，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard the news, he was just eating green-soaked melons from the Western Park; he threw them onto the platter and could not overcome his grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard the news, he was just eating green-soaked melons from the Western Park. He threw them onto the platter and could not overcome his grief.

sentences.zh: 因屈指曰：「昉少時常恐不滿五十，今四十九，可謂知命。」

translations.literal: Thereupon counting on his fingers he said, "Fang in youth often feared he would not reach fifty; now he is forty-nine—one may call this knowing fate."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon counting on his fingers he said, "Fang in youth often feared he would not reach fifty. Now he is forty-nine—one may call this knowing fate."

sentences.zh: 即日舉哀，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: That same day he raised mourning and wept for him with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he raised mourning and wept for him with extreme grief.

sentences.zh: 追贈太常，諡曰敬子。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the office of Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Respectful Son.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the office of Minister of Ceremonies. His posthumous title was Respectful Son.

sentences.zh: 昉好交結，獎進士友，不附之者亦不稱述，得其延譽者多見升擢，故衣冠貴遊莫不多與交好，坐上客恒有數十。

translations.literal: Fang loved to form connections, encouraged and advanced scholar-friends; those who did not attach to him he also did not praise; many who received his extended reputation were seen promoted; therefore the gentry and noble wanderers mostly formed friendship with him, and guests at his seat constantly numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Fang loved to form connections and encouraged and advanced scholar-friends. Those who did not attach to him he also did not praise. Many who received his extended reputation were promoted. Therefore the gentry and noble wanderers mostly formed friendship with him, and guests at his seat constantly numbered several tens.

sentences.zh: 時人慕之，號曰任君，言如漢之三君也。

translations.literal: Men of the time admired him and called him Lord Ren, meaning like the Three Lords of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time admired him and called him Lord Ren, meaning like the Three Lords of Han.

sentences.zh: 在郡尤以清潔著名，百姓年八十以上者，遣戶曹掾訪其寒溫。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was especially famed for purity and integrity; for commoners eighty years and above he sent the household registrar aide to inquire after their cold and warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he was especially famed for purity and integrity. For commoners eighty years and above he sent the household registrar aide to inquire after their welfare.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲營佛齋，調楓香二石，始入三斗，便出教長斷，曰：「與奪自己，不欲貽之後人。」

translations.literal: He once wished to hold a Buddhist fast and levied two piculs of maple incense; when only three dou had been brought in he issued an order to stop it long, saying, "Granting and taking is for oneself; I do not wish to burden later men."
translations.idiomatic: He once wished to hold a Buddhist fast and levied two piculs of maple incense. When only three dou had been brought in he issued an order to stop it, saying, "Granting and taking is for oneself. I do not wish to burden later men."

sentences.zh: 郡有蜜嶺及楊梅，舊為太守所采，昉以冒險多物故，即時停絕，吏人咸以百餘年未之有也。

translations.literal: The commandery had Honey Ridge and bayberry groves that in old times the grand administrator harvested; Fang because of the danger and many accidents immediately stopped it; officials and people all considered that in more than a hundred years there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had Honey Ridge and bayberry groves that in old times the grand administrator harvested. Fang because of the danger and many accidents immediately stopped it. Officials and people all considered that in more than a hundred years there had been nothing like it.

sentences.zh: 為家誡，殷勤甚有條貫。

translations.literal: He wrote a Family Admonition, earnest and very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a Family Admonition, earnest and very well ordered.

sentences.zh: 陳郡殷芸與建安太守到溉書曰：「哲人云亡，儀錶長謝。

translations.literal: Yin Yun of Chen commandery wrote to the grand administrator of Jian'an, Dao Gai, saying, "The wise man has passed away; his bearing and measure have long taken leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yun of Chen commandery wrote to Jian'an grand administrator Dao Gai, saying, "The wise man has passed away. His bearing and measure have long taken leave.

sentences.zh: 元龜何寄，指南何托？」

translations.literal: To what shall the divine tortoise be entrusted, to what shall the south-pointing needle be committed?"
translations.idiomatic: To what shall the divine tortoise be entrusted? To what shall the south-pointing needle be committed?"

sentences.zh: 其為士友所推如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed by scholar-friends.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he esteemed by scholar-friends.

sentences.zh: 昉不事生產，至乃居無室宅。

translations.literal: Fang did not attend to production; he even had no dwelling house.
translations.idiomatic: Fang did not attend to production and even had no dwelling house.

sentences.zh: 時或譏其多乞貸，亦隨復散之親故，常自歎曰：「知我者亦以叔則，不知我者亦以叔則。」

translations.literal: At times men mocked him for much begging and borrowing, but he also immediately distributed it again among kin and friends; he often sighed to himself, "Those who know me also take me for Shuzi; those who do not know me also take me for Shuzi."
translations.idiomatic: At times men mocked him for much begging and borrowing, but he also immediately distributed it again among kin and friends. He often sighed to himself, "Those who know me also take me for Shuzi. Those who do not know me also take me for Shuzi."

sentences.zh: 既以文才見知，時人云：「任筆沈詩」。

translations.literal: Since he was known for literary talent, men of the time said, "Ren's brush, Shen's poetry."
translations.idiomatic: Since he was known for literary talent, men of the time said, "Ren's brush, Shen's poetry."

sentences.zh: 昉聞甚以為病。

translations.literal: "When Fang heard this he took it very much as an affliction.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang heard this he took it very much as an affliction.

sentences.zh: 晚節轉好著詩，欲以傾沈，用事過多，屬辭不得流便，自爾都下士子慕之，轉為穿鑿，於是有才盡之談矣。

translations.literal: In his later years he turned to liking to compose poetry, wishing to overturn Shen; he used allusions too heavily and his phrasing could not flow smoothly; from then the gentlemen of the capital admired this and turned to forced elaboration; thereby arose talk that talent was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to composing poetry, wishing to overturn Shen. He used allusions too heavily and his phrasing could not flow smoothly. From then the gentlemen of the capital admired this and turned to forced elaboration, and thereby arose talk that talent was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 博學，於書無所不見，家雖貧，聚書至萬餘卷，率多異本。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned; in books there was nothing he had not seen; though his family was poor, he collected books to more than ten thousand scrolls, mostly variant editions.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned. In books there was nothing he had not seen. Though his family was poor, he collected books to more than ten thousand scrolls, mostly variant editions.

sentences.zh: 及卒後，武帝使學士賀縱共沈約勘其書目，官無者就其家取之。

translations.literal: After his death the Emperor sent the academicians He Zong and Shen Yue jointly to collate his book catalogue; what the office lacked they took from his household.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Emperor sent the academicians He Zong and Shen Yue jointly to collate his book catalogue. What the office lacked they took from his household.

sentences.zh: 所著文章數十萬言，盛行于時。

translations.literal: The writings he composed numbered several hundred thousand words and flourished in his time.
translations.idiomatic: The writings he composed numbered several hundred thousand words and flourished in his time.

sentences.zh: 東海王僧孺嘗論之，以為「過於董生、揚子。

translations.literal: Wang Sengru of Donghai once discussed him, considering that he "surpassed Master Dong and Master Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru of Donghai once discussed him, considering that he "surpassed Master Dong and Master Yang.

sentences.zh: 昉樂人之樂，憂人之憂，虛往實歸，忘貧去吝，行可以厲風俗，義可以厚人倫，能使貪夫不取，懦夫有立」。

translations.literal: Fang rejoiced in others' joy and grieved in others' grief; he went empty and returned full, forgot poverty and cast off stinginess; his conduct could sharpen custom, his righteousness could thicken human bonds; he could make the greedy not take and the timid stand firm."
translations.idiomatic: Fang rejoiced in others' joy and grieved in others' grief. He went empty-handed and returned enriched, forgot poverty and cast off stinginess. His conduct could sharpen custom, his righteousness could thicken human bonds. He could make the greedy refrain from taking and the timid stand firm."

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he esteemed.

sentences.zh: 有子東裏、西華、南容、北叟，並無術業，墜其家聲。

translations.literal: He had sons Dongli, Xihua, Nanrong, and Beisou, all without learning or accomplishment, who brought down the family's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Dongli, Xihua, Nanrong, and Beisou, all without learning or accomplishment, who brought down the family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 兄弟流離不能自振，生平舊交莫有收恤。

translations.literal: The brothers wandered destitute and could not revive themselves; none of his old friends of a lifetime came to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers wandered destitute and could not revive themselves. None of his old friends of a lifetime came to their aid.

sentences.zh: 西華冬月著葛帔綀裙，道逢平原劉孝標，泫然矜之，謂曰：「我當為卿作計。」

translations.literal: In winter Xihua wore a hemp cape and silk-lined skirt; on the road he met Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan, who wept and pitied him, saying, "I shall make a plan for you."
translations.idiomatic: In winter Xihua wore a hemp cape and silk-lined skirt. On the road he met Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan, who wept and pitied him, saying, "I shall make a plan for you."

sentences.zh: 乃著廣絕交論以譏其舊交曰：

translations.literal: He thereupon composed the Treatise on Severing Friendships Broadly to satirize his old friends, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon composed the Treatise on Severing Friendships Broadly to satirize his old friends, saying:

sentences.zh: 客問主人曰：「朱公叔絕交論，為是乎，為非乎？」

translations.literal: The guest asked the host, "Zhu Gongshu's Treatise on Severing Friendships—is it right or wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: The guest asked the host, "Zhu Gongshu's Treatise on Severing Friendships—is it right or wrong?"

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「客奚此之問？」

translations.literal: The host said, "Guest, why this question?"
translations.idiomatic: The host said, "Guest, why this question?"

sentences.zh: 客曰：「夫草蟲鳴則阜螽躍，雕虎嘯而清風起，故氛氳相感，霧湧雲蒸，嚶鳴相召，星流電激。

translations.literal: The guest said, "When the grass insects cry, the locusts leap; when the carved tiger roars, the clear wind rises. Thus vapors respond to one another, mist wells up and clouds steam; chirping calls to chirping, stars stream and lightning flashes.
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "When the grass insects cry, the locusts leap. When the carved tiger roars, the clear wind rises. Thus vapors respond to one another, mist wells up and clouds steam. Chirping calls to chirping, stars stream and lightning flashes.

sentences.zh: 是以王陽登則貢公喜，罕生逝而國子悲。

translations.literal: Therefore when Wang Yang ascended, Duke Gong rejoiced; when Hansheng passed away, Guozi grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Wang Yang ascended, Duke Gong rejoiced. When Hansheng passed away, Guozi grieved.

sentences.zh: 且心同琴瑟，言鬱鬱于蘭茞，道協膠漆，志婉孌於塤篪。

translations.literal: Moreover hearts are like zither and lute; words flourish richly as orchid and angelica; the Way agrees like glue and lacquer; wills twine tenderly as xun and chi flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover hearts are like zither and lute. Words flourish richly as orchid and angelica. The Way agrees like glue and lacquer. Wills twine tenderly as xun and chi flutes.

sentences.zh: 聖賢以此鏤金板而鐫盤盂，書玉牒而刻鍾鼎。

translations.literal: Sages and worthies for this carved gold boards and engraved platters and bowls, wrote jade tablets and cut bell and tripod inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Sages and worthies for this carved gold boards and engraved platters and bowls, wrote jade tablets and cut bell and tripod inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 若乃匠石輟成風之妙巧，伯牙息流波之雅引，范、張款款於下泉，尹、班陶陶於永夕。

translations.literal: As for Craftsman Shi ceasing his marvelous skill of the completed wind, Boya laying aside the elegant melody of Flowing Waves, Fan and Zhang earnest in the lower spring, Yin and Ban at ease through the long night.
translations.idiomatic: As for Craftsman Shi ceasing his marvelous skill of the completed wind, Boya laying aside the elegant melody of Flowing Waves, Fan and Zhang earnest in the lower spring, Yin and Ban at ease through the long night.

sentences.zh: 駱驛從橫，煙霏雨散，巧曆所不知，心計莫能測。

translations.literal: They come and go in file, mist scatters like rain; what clever reckoners do not know, what the mind's plans cannot measure.
translations.idiomatic: They come and go in file, mist scatters like rain. What clever reckoners do not know, what the mind's plans cannot measure.

sentences.zh: 而朱益州汨彝敘，粵謨訓，捶直切，絕交遊，視黔首以鷹鸇，媲人靈於豺虎。

translations.literal: Yet the Administrator of Yizhou Zhu muddies the Yi narrative, in Yue mode admonishes and instructs, beats straight and cuts off, severs friendly intercourse, views the black-haired people as hawks and falcons, and compares human spirits to jackals and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Administrator Zhu of Yizhou muddies the Yi narrative, admonishes in Yue mode, beats straight and cuts off, severs friendly intercourse, views the common people as hawks and falcons, and compares human spirits to jackals and tigers.

sentences.zh: 蒙有猜焉，請辯其惑。」

translations.literal: I have doubts about this; please resolve my confusion."
translations.idiomatic: I have doubts about this. Please resolve my confusion."

sentences.zh: 主人聽然曰：「客所謂撫弦徽音，未達燥濕變響，張羅沮澤，不睹鴻雁高飛。

translations.literal: The host listened and said, "What the guest calls stroking the strings for clear tone has not reached the changing sound of dry and wet; spreading nets in marshy ground does not see the wild geese flying high.
translations.idiomatic: The host listened and said, "What you call stroking the strings for clear tone has not reached the changing sound of dry and wet. Spreading nets in marshy ground does not see the wild geese flying high.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖人握金鏡，闡風烈，龍驤蠖屈，從道汙隆。

translations.literal: The sage holds the golden mirror, unfolds wind and blazing merit; the dragon rears, the silkworm curls, following the Way in rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: The sage holds the golden mirror and unfolds wind and blazing merit. The dragon rears, the silkworm curls, following the Way in rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 日月連璧，贊亹亹之弘致，雲飛雷薄，顯棣華之微旨。
